catalog.purpose: Actual Google TCMalloc snapshot, default 8 KiB page configuration, statically linked with its exact Bazel-selected Abseil object closure. Qualified on Linux x86_64 with GCC 13.3.0 and GNU C++11 ABI: fresh consumer compilation, 8-thread malloc/calloc/realloc and ownership/size checks, 24000 allocation rounds, 4096 cross-thread frees, aligned and C++ allocation, 16 MiB live-byte accounting, sampling configuration, stats and release-to-system API, semantic extension-only negative control, missing-library and mismatched-ABI rejection, and executable malloc symbol/load provenance. Per-CPU caches were inactive on the acceptance host. No per-CPU performance, upstream full test suite, alternative allocator configuration, dynamic loading or stable ABI qualification is claimed. Three documented GCC13 class-memaccess diagnostics remain warnings in only the observed translation units; upstream source bytes are unchanged.

runtime_requirements: Linux x86_64; this binary payload is a toolchain-specific static archive.
glibc satisfying recorded ELF version requirements: maximum GLIBC version required by the freshly linked acceptance consumer is GLIBC_2.38.
libstdc++.so.6 providing GLIBCXX_3.4.32 and CXXABI_1.3.8; libgcc_s.so.1 providing GCC_3.4.
GNU g++ with C++17 and _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1; GCC 13.3.0 was actually used and qualified.
Python 3.12 or newer; GNU nm and readelf, and ldd are required for functional acceptance.
LD_PRELOAD must be unset; do not combine this snapshot with another TCMalloc or Abseil ABI.

Offline source replay additionally requires gcc, GNU ar and ranlib, shell tools, and a fresh writable work directory; fixed Bazel 8.8.2 and target-specific vendored dependencies are included in the companion.
Validated on Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.39; no lower ABI bound is inferred. Exact ELF requirements are recorded separately.
